checked_claims.note: For smooth complex DM stacks over Q, H_k^{BM}(X) ≅ H^{2d-k}(X)(d) as MHS. With d=21 and k=16 this is H^{26}(X)(21); twisting by (21) shifts weights by -42, so W_{-16}H_16^{BM} ≅ W_26 H^{26}(X)(21). Stack vs coarse is harmless over Q. Matches FND-0001 arithmetic; not restated as a new finding.

Localization H^{15}(D)→H_c^{16}(X)→H^{16}(Y)→H^{16}(D) is exact in MHS. Weight bounds: D proper ⇒ weights on H^{15}(D) ≤15; Y smooth proper ⇒ H^{16}(Y) pure of weight 16; X smooth ⇒ weights on H_c^{16} ≤16. Then W_15 H_c ⊆ ker(β) by purity of the target, ker(β)=im(α) by exactness, and im(α)⊆W_15 by source weights, so ker=W_15 and Gr^W_16 H_c^{16} ≅ K:=ker(H^{16}(Y)→H^{16}(D)) as pure HS of weight 16.
H_k^{BM} ≅ (H_c^k)^vee as MHS in the same degree (no extra Tate twist). With weights on H_c^{16} ≤16, W_{-16}H_16^{BM} ≅ (Gr^W_16 H_c^{16})^vee. Dual of Q(-8) is Q(8).

Each one-edge clutching factors through D (finite quotients of clutching sources onto boundary components). Hence K ⊆ P. Only the inclusion is used; reverse inclusion is not claimed. Finite stabilizers/graph automorphisms over Q are fine for this inclusion.

The even boundary-detection lemma is not established. Fatal gaps: (i) the ordered stable-arc complex is never identified with a resolution of the simultaneous restriction kernels defining P; (ii) the proposed homotopy h is only a combinatorial arc-insertion rule with no defined action on Künneth decorations, so dh+hd=id is not an identity on the written complex; (iii) the sketch mixes degree-preserving restriction pullbacks ξ_Γ^* (which define P) with node/Gysin shifts (wrong complex); (iv) genus ≥2 non-Tate decorations that already lie in a vertex-level restriction kernel are terminals that h cannot kill, and no induction on (g,n) is supplied; (v) the bound m≤2g+n-2 is not used in the body, which instead jumps from m<22 to m≤16 without justification. Semisimplicity would upgrade a genuine non-Tate vanishing of P to Tate type, but that vanishing is not proved.
K ⊆ P and semisimplicity of pure polarizable HS would give that any subobject of a Tate sum is Tate, but Tate-ness of P (C3) failed, so Tate-ness of K remains unsettled by the writeup.
Target needs C2 (confirmed) plus Tate-ness of K (unresolved). Dualities would correctly send Q(-8)^⊕r to Q(8)^⊕r if K were Tate; that step is not reached.

finding_candidates.evidence: H^m(Y) pure of weight m; weights on H^{m-1}(D) ≤ m-1 (D proper); weights on H_c^m(X) ≤ m (X smooth); morphisms of MHS preserve W so W_{m-1}H_c ⊆ ker(β); exactness gives ker(β)=im(α) ⊆ W_{m-1}; hence ker=W_{m-1} and Gr_m H_c ≅ im(β)=ker(H^m(Y)→H^m(D)).

finding_candidates.statement: For X=M_{g,n} smooth, Y=overline{M}_{g,n} smooth proper, D=Y\X proper, and coefficients Q, localization plus Deligne weight bounds give Gr^W_m H_c^m(X;Q) ≅ ker(H^m(Y;Q)→H^m(D;Q)) as pure polarizable HS of weight m; in particular for (g,n,m)=(6,6,16).

finding_candidates.evidence: ATT-0037 Section 2 defines h by flag-ordered arc insertion and claims dh+hd=id after Tate quotient, but generators carry vertex cohomology decorations; clutching pullback goes cut→uncut and does not split on cohomology in general; classes already in a vertex-level P are sent to 0 by any pullback-based h, so they are unaccounted terminals of genus possibly ≥2.

scope.applies_to: attempts proving low-degree boundary-restriction kernels of H^*(overline M_{g,n}) are Tate

finding_candidates.statement: A purely combinatorial ordered-arc insertion operator does not supply a chain homotopy on the Künneth-decorated one-edge restriction complex: without a cohomological rule for how vertex classes transform under arc insertion, and without a comparison theorem identifying the arc complex with the restriction/Čech complex for clutching maps, one cannot conclude that the simultaneous one-edge kernel P^m_{g,n} is Tate.

finding_candidates.evidence: P is defined by ξ_Γ^* (same cohomological degree m). Gysin maps shift degree by 2 per edge and introduce Tate twists (-1). ATT-0037 simultaneously defines P via pullbacks and invokes node shifts in the terminal-degree parity argument.
finding_candidates.statement: Degree counts that invoke per-edge node/Gysin shifts analyze a different complex (Gysin/weight spectral sequence or boundary-pushforward span) from the simultaneous kernel of degree-preserving clutching pullbacks ξ_Γ^*; conclusions about one do not transfer to the other without a duality reindexing that changes the degree being studied.

proof_dependency_checks.note: Deligne MHS, weight bounds for proper/smooth sources, strictness, Poincare/BM dualities over Q on smooth DM stacks (via level covers + invariants) are correctly applied in Section 1; equation (1) Gr^W_16 H_c^{16} ≅ K stands.

Load-bearing dependency for Tate-ness of P. Discharge fails: no comparison identifying the ordered stable-arc complex with the Čech/restriction complex for one-edge clutchings; contracting homotopy not defined on decorated generators; Gysin/node-shift degree bookkeeping is incompatible with the restriction definition of P; stabilization/omitted-unstable cancellation and graph-automorphism signs are only asserted.

Eichler–Shimura first non-Tate genus-one primitives in odd degree near a=11 is standard in outline, but is only reached after the arc-complex model equals P. Not independently verified in full local-system precision here; non-load-bearing once the arc resolution fails.

strongest_attack: The attempt reduces the target correctly to Tate-ness of K=ker(H^{16}(Ȳ)→H^{16}(D)) via PD/BM dualities and weight-strict localization, and K⊆P is fine, but Tate-ness of P rests on an ordered stable-arc contraction that is not a proof: h is undefined on Künneth decorations (so dh+hd=id fails for any class already in a vertex-level restriction kernel), the complex is never shown to compute the restriction kernels defining P, and node/Gysin shifts are conflated with degree-preserving clutching pullbacks—leaving genus ≥2 non-Tate summands uncontrolled at m=16. Outcome: Section 1 confirmed; claimed completeness of the theorem fails at Section 2 (incomplete, not a clean theorem refutation).
theorem_statement: The exact group W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q), equivalently W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21), is a direct sum of Q(8); a disproof must exhibit a surviving non-Tate summand in this exact group.
